title: Research Projects
text: My research projects focus on the molecular underpinnings of respiratory and autoimmune diseases using multi-omics approaches. All code and analysis pipelines are publicly available on GitHub.

title: Research Projects
text:
Interstitial Lung Disease — BAL scRNA-seq (2025)

Single-cell RNA sequencing of bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid from patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD). This project characterises alveolar immune cell populations in pulmonary fibrosis and identifies novel transcriptomic signatures associated with disease progression.
View on GitHub →

title: Research Projects
text:
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus — Ancestry Methylation (2023)

Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis of buffy coat samples from African American and European American cohorts with SLE and lupus nephritis. Identified ancestry-specific epigenetic signatures and interferon pathway enrichment driving disease heterogeneity.
View on GitHub →

title: Research Projects
text:
Scleroderma — Monocyte Methylation (2023)

Genome-wide DNA methylation and gene expression profiling of classical monocytes in African American patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc). Characterised distinct epigenetic signatures distinguishing SSc monocytes from healthy controls.
View on GitHub →

title: Dr Peter C. Allen
text:
Biomedical researcher with specialised expertise in single-cell genomics, epigenetics, and computational analysis of immune and respiratory disease. PhD-trained in genetics with subsequent postdoctoral experience leading computational analyses of interstitial lung disease (ILD) at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Sydney.
Co-first author of a comprehensive pan-ILD single-cell atlas of bronchoalveolar lavage and contributor to multiple high-impact manuscripts in Nature and other peer-reviewed journals. Recipient of competitive national research funding and a national society award for excellence in oral presentation.

title: Dr Peter C. Allen
text:
Research Interests

Technical Expertise
Computational and bioinformatic: single-cell RNA sequencing analysis; single-cell ATAC sequencing analysis; multi-omic data integration; gene regulatory network inference; differential expression and trajectory analysis; whole-genome and epigenome-wide association studies; pipeline development (Nextflow, Snakemake); high-performance and cloud computing.
Programming: R, Python, Bash, Git.
Wet-lab: methylation-specific assay development; cell-based immune modification (CAR-T background); tissue processing for clinical-grade allograft applications.
Disease areas: interstitial lung disease, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, Epstein-Barr virus-related lymphomas.

title: Events
text:
19–21 May 2025 · Sydney, Australia
As host and organiser, I brought together experimental (wet-lab) and computational (dry-lab) scientists for three days of intensive collaboration on outstanding challenges in single-cell multiomics. The event ran right into the Oz Single Cell 2025 Conference.
Programme:

Mon 19 May (9am–6pm) — Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Auditorium
Tue 20 May (9am–5pm) — The Kinghorn Cancer Centre
Wed 21 May (9am–11am) — Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Auditorium (results presentation)

Focus: scMultiome integration challenges — tackling batch correction, multi-modal data integration, and cell-type annotation across large-scale single-cell datasets.
The hackathon aimed to seed new projects and collaborations, produce new tools for single-cell data visualisation and analysis, and contribute to a Grand Challenges summary publication.

title: Events
text:
CREATE Genomics Workshop 2024
25 July 2024 · Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Sydney
I delivered a hands-on demonstration on analysing ILD bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) scRNA-seq data, covering the full analysis pipeline from raw data to annotated cell populations.
Topics covered:

Overview — Why single-cell RNA sequencing? Capturing cellular heterogeneity and sub-lineages lost in bulk sequencing; ILD cohort of 33 BAL samples across 3 phases including IPF, HP, SR-ILD, Silicosis, NSIP, and PPFE
Quality Control — UMI count filtering, ambient RNA removal (SoupX/CellBender), mitochondrial percentage thresholds, batch effect assessment
Integration — Multi-sample integration using scVI and Harmony/Seurat to separate biological signal from batch artefact; gene expression normalisation (shifted logarithm)
Clustering — Grouping cells by expression profile using Leiden, Louvain, and K-means algorithms
Annotation — Automated annotation with Azimuth, Celltypist, and Scimilarity; manual annotation using known cell-type marker genes

Note: a live coding demonstration accompanied these slides; recording is unavailable.
